emily: Drafting a concise 429 troubleshooting runbook for Troubleshooting -> Errors. Need tiny curl, python, node snippets + a 1-line SDK v0.11 migration note. Who can drop snippets? :wave:
sam: I can do Python. Will show parsing Retry-After then fallback to exponential jitter. Keep it tiny.
matt: I'll add a curl streaming example and one-line advice: prefer Retry-After header when present. Also a fallback sentence about routing to cheaper model if sustained.
irene: Found an old link in /guides/limits. I'll update to https://redwood.ai/docs/limits#too-many-requests in the PR.
sam: Python snippet:
```python
# prefer Retry-After header, else exponential backoff + jitter
import time, random
for i in range(5):
    r = client.generate(... )
    if r.status_code == 429:
        ra = int(r.headers.get('Retry-After', 0))
        if ra:
            time.sleep(ra)
        else:
            time.sleep((2 ** i) * 0.5 + random.random() * 0.25)
        continue
    break
```
matt: curl streaming example:
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"xlarge","prompt":"...","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# on 429: check Retry-After or X-RateLimit-Reset; consider fallback to a smaller model or cached prefix
```
emily: SDK migration blurb (v0.10 -> v0.11):
```python
# v0.10
resp = client.generate(prompt, max_context=4096)
# v0.11
resp = client.generate(prompt, context_limit=4096, auto_trim=True)
```
